body:
when popover / popovertarget were being created this use case was discussed.  but one of the reasons why it wasn't included in the initial implementations for these attributes, is because there's a lot more that needs to be considered to get this sort of markup pattern done correctly for a11y/common ux expectations.

some of the functionality you mention "typing in to search and the list of items get filtered matching the search" is out of scope behavior for popover.  Additionally, there are quite a few additional considerations an author would need to script to properly associated the popover with the text field for keyboard / general accessibility expectations for such widgets.   None of these behaviors being 100% consistent depending on the type of popover the text field might be invoking (e.g., a listbox vs dialog vs grid - to reference the allowed widget types that a combobox can invoke per the ARIA spec).  

So, to circle back to your question:
>As far as I can see the spec doesn't exclude other input types (or does it?)

The spec only allows popovers to be declaratively invoked from buttons.  That's not to say it's not unreasonable to want/expect popovers to be invoked from other elements as well, but invoking from other elements requires additional considerations to ensure such popovers would be accessible to all users.  All I can say for now is that this desire is not lost of anyone who worked on popover, it's just not presently a reality for a number of good reasons.

However, you _can_ use JavaScript to invoke a popover from a text field, which per all the stuff I mentioned, you're going to have to be writing a lot of extra JS for this anyway to properly implement for expected ux/a11y, so that shouldn't be a blocker in the grand scheme of things.

I hope this explanation was helpful.

Thanks, these are all fair points you make, and I'm glad it was discussed at time of creation.

> some of the functionality you mention "typing in to search and the list of items get filtered matching the search" is out of scope behavior for popover.

Definitely, but was just one example of an implementation. Though for that same reason (advanced behaviour being out of scope of Popover API), that indicates Popover API shouldn't have to care about the pandoras box of additional considerations of popover types. The primitives are provided to make it work and if that's my use case for the implementation I need then I'll write that in and make those considerations.

To me (who admittedly does not have the full context of the discussion or wider impacts) it seemed unnecessarily restrictive to limit that behaviour to only one specific type of input

This desire was initially borne out of a frustration where I had implemented various popovers for buttons and inputs, then spent a long time debugging why it wasn't working for one particular input I had created. I won't admit how long it took me to realise it was the `type="search"` that was the problem! (the other inputs were already type="button" as they were existing implementations using a different approach to provide popover-like behaviour)

(To defend myself though, MDN docs currently show this - the type="button" detail only provided when diving in deeper on the details.)
![Screenshot 2024-12-04 at 12 36 14 pm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0eb3992a-8d25-4339-a9dd-4514068f86ac)

> However, you can use JavaScript to invoke a popover from a text field

yeah, this is how I deal with it currently, seems to work well (and allows me to open it on focus - which I guess would be one of those additional considerations you mentioned 😉 )

> you're going to have to be writing a lot of extra JS for this anyway to properly implement for expected ux/a11y

Wasn't as much as you might think thanks to floating-ui

> All I can say for now is that this desire is not lost of anyone who worked on popover, it's just not presently a reality for a number of good reasons.

Totally, and it's wholly awesome. This is a minor nitpick :)

Appreciate your time, thanks!
Happy for this to be closed and with the issue kept here as a reference or point of discussion
